source_text: Anatomically, male circumcision removes a fold of skin (the foreskin) that protects the glans but does not fundamentally alter penile erectile, urinary, or sensory functions, whereas infibulation excises the clitoris—the primary site of female sexual pleasure and orgasm—and constructs a barrier that impedes natural vaginal function, often requiring repeated cutting for intercourse or childbirth. [92]
